To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we determined the crystal structures of Shark and Sus TCB1D15 GAPs and found that they both have higher activity on Rab11 than Rab7.
the Shark and Sus GAP domains have a conserved structure with other TBC domain‐bearing Rab GAPs.
the Shark and Sus GAP domains have a similar structure to the yeast Gyp1 Rab GAP domain, and they both have a higher catalytic activity for Rab11a than Rab7a.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of Shark TBC1D5 GAP and Sus TBC GAP, and the catalytic mechanism of Shark TBC GAP and Sus GAP on Rab GTPase.
the catalytic mechanism of Shark and Sus T‐BC1D15 on Rab GTPase.
the structure and activity of Shark and Sus TPC1D15 GAPs, and provides new insights into the catalytic mechanism of TBC1 family GAPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Shark‐TBC GAP and Sus‐TBD GAP are highly similar and both are specific for Rab11a.
the TBC1 domain of Shark GAP and TBC1 domain Sus GAP can activate the Rab GTPases by hydrolyzing their GTPs.
the Shark and Sus GAP structures represent new members of the TBC GAP domain family, which may have different catalytic mechanisms from other GAPs, and they may be specific to Rab11.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Shark and Sus GAP domains are conserved in structure and catalytic activity on different Rab GTPases.
the crystal structures of TBC1 D15 GAP domain and its catalytic mechanism have been solved.
Shark‐TBC and Sus‐Tbc1d GAP domains have a conserved structure and are both active on Rab11a and Rab7a.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Shark and Sus Tbc1d15 are highly conserved in structure and function.
Shark‐TBC‐1D15 and its homologs are GAPs for Rab11a and Rab7a, and that the GAP domain is highly conserved.
Shark GAP and Sus TBC GAP domains are evolutionally conserved and have higher catalytic activities on Rab11a.
